questions.question: R² = 0.82 means...
options: 82% of the points lie on the line
The line accounts for 82% of the variation in y
The prediction is wrong 18% of the time
questions.explanation: R² is the share of the total variation in y that the regression line explains. The rest is left in the residuals.

questions.question: A scatter plot shows a clear curve, yet R² for a straight line is 0.95. What should you conclude?
options: The line is a great model
R² can be high even when a straight line is the wrong shape, so check the residuals
R² must have been computed wrongly
The data are not suitable for any model
questions.explanation: R² only measures tightness around the line. A curved pattern can still give a high R², and shows up as a U shape in the residual plot.

questions.question: SST = 798 and SSE = 141.9. What is R²?
questions.explanation: SSR = 798 − 141.9 = 656.1 and R² = 656.1 ÷ 798 = 0.822. (0.907 is r, and 0.178 is the share left unexplained.)

questions.question: In simple linear regression, how are R² and the correlation r related?
questions.explanation: In simple regression R² is the square of the correlation coefficient. With r = 0.907, R² = 0.822.

questions.question: A residual plot shows points spreading out wider and wider as x increases. What is violated?
options: The mean of the residuals is zero
questions.explanation: A fan shape means the spread of the residuals changes with x: unequal variance, or heteroscedasticity.

questions.question: Adding one student (9 hours, score 30) changes the slope from 3.95 to 0.43. This point is...
options: An influential point: high leverage and a huge residual
Proof that studying does not work
questions.explanation: The point is far out in x (high leverage) and far from the line in y (big residual), so it pulls the whole line toward itself.

questions.question: For a given x, how do a 95% confidence interval for the mean response and a 95% prediction interval for one new case compare?
questions.explanation: The prediction interval adds the individual's own scatter (the '1 +' term), so it is always wider than the confidence interval for the mean.

questions.question: Which action is appropriate when you find an influential point?
options: Delete it silently to improve R²
Investigate it and report the analysis with and without it
questions.explanation: Check whether it is an error or a real case, and be transparent about its effect. Quietly deleting data is not acceptable.
